system.summary: Numerical syllabary of the Spanish embassy at Genoa, 1577: a numeral is a consonant, a mark after it the vowel (cross a, dot e, 6-loop i, hook o, stroke u), bare 10/4/2/18/1 the vowels, marks above add n, s, r or l; code groups carry a small cross above (145 V.Md., 8 + hook Señoria, 6 + hook republica). Inline in clear Spanish.
system.notes: Key: K_P2 of Brice Dudout (targets/perez1578/key.tsv), with 8 = b as his notes give for the Genoa table, frozen before decrypting. Seen here but not in the key: tilde over 33, underline (perhaps r -> l), small 2 above, dot after vowel 2, code 30. underlined. 35 + hook read pri once (a marked repair). key_frozen.tsv holds 49 entries on 56 lines (7 comment lines): 5 bare vowels, 27 consonant numerals, 5 vowel marks, 4 superscript marks, 1 special sign, 7 code groups.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment filed with the letter; no edition found in two web searches (12 Nov 2026); not in Dan's repo (origin/main 65445e3f8).

solution.what: [Don John letters, PR #593] PARES full-text search "copia de carta de Juan de Austria": 1410,111 (decipherment of 1410,77, 6 Aug 1577) and 1410,110 (decipherment of the 7 Aug letter) found, neither linked to a cipher.

[Don John letters, PR #593] The Genoa 1577 key (K5, validated on the pair 1410,78/79: 87.3% words, 95.5% characters) adapted to the hand of 1410,77 on 1410,77 lines 1-24 against 1410,111; held-out 1410,77 page 3 against 1410,111 page 3: 57.9% words, 72.7% characters, 200 controls at most 27.1 / 49.2 (old transcription at 1011 px).
PARES record 3577720: viewer page, 8 images at zoom 10 and the description page; 1414,4 (3549587): viewer and 4 images. 15 requests, one at a time, 6-9 s apart, no 429.
Sign conventions by shape; two independent passes of the 26 cipher lines of images 1-2; reconciled on zooms.
K_P2 (Brice Dudout, from cipher/descifrada pairs of AGS Estado 1410) frozen with the Genoa-table value 8 = b before decryption (SHA-256 in key_frozen.sha256).

Whole passage held out from the key. Frozen key: 97.0% of characters and 91.0% of 122 words (3+ letters; 111 of 122) agree with the reading; 200 permuted-key controls at most 92.2% / 74.6% (mean 8.0% words). The reference is the reading itself, so the test is not independent of it.

Mechanical decryption read as Spanish with every departure marked; check_marks.py passes. 187 cipher words: 173 verbatim, 3 repaired, 3 guesses, 8 holes. Dan's docs/_check_reading.py: reading_1410_115.md readable, clean share 0.727 (16 of 22 sentences).
Two web searches on the letter, the ambassadors, Genoa 1577 and the French ambassador; no edition or decipherment found.

Independent blind review: 4 lines of image 2 (68 signs) read by shape before opening the transcription, 64 agree; mark check, decryption and held-out test rerun; state read in part confirmed, grade B. After it, one shape read 11 in all 4 places (two repairs became verbatim readings) and the English of the first sentence aligned with the reading.

Integration check (round 7): reran decrypt/check_marks/heldout (0.970 and 0.910 of 122 words, controls at most 0.922 and 0.746), _check_reading (0.727) and _check_profile; own second decoder from key_frozen.tsv gives an identical decryption; key_frozen hash matches and agrees with perez1578 K_P2 apart from the changes the notes give. PARES returned 429 to the checking session, so no image comparison. Status set to in progress: images 3-6 (about 105 cipher lines) are not transcribed, a workable gap.

[Don John letters, PR #593] Key extended on the already-used 77/111 data only (xil gente, sim mente, pam nuestro, pam+ nuestra, yum+ otra, 26 = v, bare 6 = i) and frozen (donjuan/key_frozen.json, SHA-256 in donjuan/key_frozen.sha256) before 1410,135 was transcribed.

[Don John letters, PR #593] 1410,135 found to be the cipher of 1410,110 from its cipher heading ("copia de carta del señor [don Juan] para los embaxadores de Genova del castillo de Namur a 7 de agosto 1577"). Body transcribed in two passes and frozen (SHA-256 3558ee69...) before 1410,110 was opened.

[Don John letters, PR #593] One measurement, donjuan/scripts/heldout.py: frozen key on 1410,135 against 1410,110 = 80.2% of 106 words, 89.2% of 437 characters; 200 controls (100 permuted consonant values, 100 shuffled unit orders) at most 18.9% / 47.8%. Criterion written beforehand (characters >= 0.85 and >= best control + 0.30): met.

[Don John letters, PR #593] The decryption follows 1410,110 word for word; the misses are signs of the copy (26 = fi here, 14 written with a cross, an+ for on) and words the cipher has and the decipherment drops ("que cada dia" before "se ofrecen").

Integration check of PR #593 and fold of targets/donjuan1577 into this folder as donjuan/ (one key, one entry): heldout.py rerun (0.802 words, 0.892 characters; 200 controls at most 0.189 / 0.478); both SHA-256 values match; own second decoder from donjuan/key_frozen.json identical to the contributor's decryption; the key agrees with this folder's key_frozen.tsv on 30 of 31 shared syllabary signs (26 differs) and with perez1578/key.tsv on 64 of 69. PARES returned 429, so no image comparison; the pairing 1410,77 / 1410,111 is by the contributor's record.

texts.label: AGS Estado 1410,115, cipher of images 1-2
texts.summary: The ambassadors play down the report that the French will send an ordinary ambassador to Genoa: perhaps the Count of [Fiesco] and some exiles of the conspiracy or their relatives pressed for it, but it is no general request of the 'new' nobles, whose leading men now make one body with the 'old'; if a French ambassador could ever be kept out it is now, though Genoa is too changeable to promise anything. On the conspiracy, they gave the Signoria the King's letter on investigating it and punishing the guilty.
texts.note: Images 1-2 only (26 of about 130 cipher lines). 187 cipher words: 173 verbatim from the signs (92.5%), 3 with a marked repair, 3 guesses (Fiesco, llaman, mucho), 8 holes (signs with marks the key does not give, among them acá and inferiores). Images 3-6 not transcribed.

reading_review.note: The five sentences build sense in 16th-century chancery Spanish, with one or two marked holes or guesses each; 4 lines of image 2 (68 signs) were read by shape before opening the transcription and 64 signs agree. Only 26 of about 130 cipher lines are read, and acá llaman is the weakest guess.
